issues.legal_issue: Execution of a final ejectment order is not barred by the passage of time when the governing scheme prescribes no time limit for execution.
material_facts: An order requiring the appellant to vacate the property became final after it was confirmed by the Supreme Court.
Execution proceedings were initiated, and the appellant objected that more than twelve years had elapsed.
The governing statutory scheme prescribed no limitation period for executing the order.
issues.conclusion: The order could be executed at any time, and the objection based on the passage of time was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21 of the Mamlatdar’s Courts Act, 1906 prescribes no limitation period for executing an order. The Court held that, in the absence of a specific limitation, the general law of limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963 is excluded by necessary implication, and no implied requirement to exercise the power within a reasonable time arises where a statutory rule governs. Babaji Khanduji v. Kushaba Ramji was relied on for the absence of a prescribed limitation period. State of Gujarat v. Patel Raghav Natha, Ram Chand v. Union of India, and Mohamad Kavi Mohamad Amin were distinguished as irrelevant to the circumstances before the Court.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party sought to enforce an order requiring another party to vacate property.
predicates.ejectment_order_final: The order requiring the occupant to vacate had become final.
predicates.governing_scheme_sets_no_execution_deadl: The rules governing enforcement set no deadline for executing the order.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to enforce a final order to vacate property under a scheme that sets no execution deadline, elapsed time does not bar execution.
